text:
maria: Heads up — saw a reproducible hang on multi-node TP runs when async all-reduce is enabled after KV-cache warmup. 4 nodes x 2 GPUs each, run config below. job stuck, one rank pinned in ncclAllReduce

ajay: Oof. Can you paste the exact run command + env?

maria: Command: `python serve.py --model gptx --tp 2 --nodes 4 --batching async`
Env: `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 NCCL_DEBUG=INFO CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1`

simon: Any stack traces? Which rank stuck? nccl logs?

maria: Rank 5 stalls. Attaching log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-18 14:02:07][rank:5] nv_peer_comm: entering ncclAllReduce
[2026-03-18 14:02:09][rank:5] nv_peer_comm: waiting on recv (timeout)
[2026-03-18 14:02:09][rank:5] ncclNet: timeout waiting for connection
```

maria: Also saw this in runtime trace: heavy wait on `cudaStreamSynchronize` inside kernel-selection path after KV cache refill.

perf-bot: Profile summary: timeline shows compute stalls overlapping with allreduce wait. 71% idle on rank5 between 14:02:06-14:02:12. Kernel selection changed to fast-fp16 path at 14:01:59.

leo: Could be a race where KV cache refill triggers an immediate broadcast while async allreduce is in-flight. If broadcast uses the same communicator object without locking we might race.

ajay: Agreed. We had similar race in 2024 where kvcache->prefetch spawned callback that launches a collective without proper stream/comm pinning. That caused hangs on NCCL when ops interleaved.

dawn: Pinging oncall (eng-sre) to triage infra/network, but this smells like runtime ordering. @infra-bot, please collect dmesg & NIC metrics from nodes 2-4.

infra-bot: Collected: /artifacts/INC-2026-1234/nic-metrics.tar.gz. No obvious link failures, small transient packet drops on node3 at 14:02:08 (0.03%).

simon: Can we repro with NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE and NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 to rule out p2p issues? Also try setting `NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0`.

maria: Running a repro now with: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 python serve.py ...` will share logs.

maria: Quick hack: disabling async allreduce via config `--batching sync` made the job continue past the stall point. So likely ordering/overlap bug.

leo: That suggests our async path doesn't respect comm epoch semantics when KV cache updates happen. Maybe kernel selection switched to a quantized kernel and that changed stream sync points.

ajay: Two concrete reproductions to try: 1) Add explicit `cudaStreamWaitEvent(allreduce_stream, kv_ready_evt)` after KV refill before launching collective. 2) Force comm to new NCCL communicator per broadcast. If 1 works, it's a stream ordering bug; if 2 works, it's comm reuse bug.

maria: I ran #1 locally (inserted stream wait) — no hang in 3 runs. Uploading diff: https://redwood.internal/diffs/kvcache-sync-fix.patch

simon: Nice. Can you also run a run with `--kernel-select conservative` to force fallback kernels? Curious whether kernel path variance matters.

maria: With conservative kernels, also no hang in 2 attempts. So both kernel + ordering interact.

leo: Hypothesis: fast fp16 kernels launch on a different stream and we weren't synchronizing before reusing communicator buffers; that leaves partial messages for NCCL and causes a deadlock on some ranks.

dawn: Proposed next steps:
- create minimal repro harness (2 nodes) that exercises KV refill + async allreduce interleave
- add stream event in runtime as hotfix and gate behind env var `RW_FIX_KVCACHE_SYNC=1`
- run nightly stress with NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE to catch other patterns
- open an incident ticket and schedule postmortem if we see more customer impact

ajay: I can own the hotfix PR. Will add test that toggles `RW_FIX_KVCACHE_SYNC` and runs 100 iterations.

maria: Assigning to ajay. Also adding a regression test in perf-suite that runs multi-node TP with random kernel selection.

perf-bot: Created perf test: `tp_kvcache_interleave` in ci/perf with 50-iters, 4-nodes. Baseline recorded.

leo: For long-term, let's add communicator lifecycle docs: when KV cache triggers collectives we should either reuse a pinned comm+stream pair or create ephemeral comms with clear ownership. I'll start a design doc.

maria: Thanks. For now the hotfix + test should reduce risk. If anyone sees similar hangs on hosted clusters, tag this thread. :thumbsup:

ajay: PR opened https://redwood.internal/prs/4821 — includes stream wait + unit test. Requesting review from simon.

simon: Reviewing now. Quick note: also add `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` in nightly to avoid silent hangs.

maria: Updated incident: INC-2026-1234 created and linked to PR.

dawn: Great work team. Moving to follow-up board.

leo: Follow-up items assigned to design board. Will drop a link when doc is ready.

maria: Closing loop here — hotfix deployed to staging, running 12h stress. Will report if any failures.

ajay: Thanks all.
